alternatives.root_cause: A bad deploy of product-catalog shipped an artifact that fails product lookups.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible shape, but a deploy at 03:17 UTC during low traffic is less likely than a flag flip, and flagd's presence in the graph makes a runtime toggle the cheaper explanation; a change log would settle it.

alternatives.root_cause: recommendation exhausted memory or threads and began failing, with product-catalog errors a downstream artifact of retry pressure.
alternatives.why_not: recommendation alerted first but product-catalog alerted too, and errors propagate toward the caller — a recommendation-local fault would not make product-catalog itself error, nor explain checkout which does not call recommendation.

verdict.summary: A feature flag toggled in flagd put product-catalog into its failure path, so product lookup calls began returning errors that propagated to recommendation and then to all its callers.
verdict.reasoning: The alerting set is exactly product-catalog plus everything that reads from it transitively (recommendation, then frontend, checkout, frontend-proxy, load-generator). recommendation alerting a minute earlier than the rest is consistent with it being the first caller to surface product-catalog errors on a tight read loop, with frontend/checkout/proxy/load-generator following on the next evaluation window. product-catalog itself alerting means it is emitting errors rather than hanging, which rules out freeze/partition and points at a fast error return, not a wait. flagd sits in this topology fanned out to ad, cart, recommendation, product-reviews and fraud-detection, and a runtime toggle changes behaviour with no deploy or config file change, which is why nothing would show in a change log. A hard fail-fast error path rather than slow responses also argues against dependency_latency or resource exhaustion.
open_questions: flagd evaluation history around 03:17 — which flag changed and to what value
product-catalog error logs: are they synthetic/injected failures or real datastore or decode errors
whether product-catalog latency stayed flat while error rate jumped (fail-fast) or rose (saturation)
whether recommendation's errors are pass-through of product-catalog RPC status codes or its own internal faults
memory/CPU of recommendation and product-catalog to exclude a leak-driven failure
